question: Vijay has ₹1218 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Ajay and Prakash and asked them to invest it at 10% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Ajay and Prakash got same amount after 14 and 15 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Vijay give to Prakash?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of shares when amounts are equal at CI = (1 + R/100)Time Diff.

Time difference = 15 − 14 = 1 year.

Ajay's Share : Prakash's Share = (1 + 10/100)¹ = 11 : 10.

Prakash's share = (10 / 21) × 1218 = 10 × 58 = ₹580.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹580.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount = ₹1218

Time for Ajay (T₁) = 14 years

Time for Prakash (T₂) = 15 years

Rate of Interest (R) = 10%

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 
 Total = ₹1218

 
• 
 
• 

 
 Ajay (Share: A)
 T = 14 yrs, R = 10%

 
 Prakash (Share: P)
 T = 15 yrs, R = 10%

 
• 
 
• 

 
 Amounts are Equal → A / P = 11 / 10

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Ajay's share be A and Prakash's share be P.

⇒ Amount of Ajay after 14 years = A × (1 + 10/100)¹⁴

⇒ Amount of Prakash after 15 years = P × (1 + 10/100)¹⁵

⇒ Since both amounts are equal:

⇒ A × (11/10)¹⁴ = P × (11/10)¹⁵

⇒ A / P = (11/10)¹⁵ − ¹⁴

⇒ A / P = 11 / 10

⇒ The ratio of shares of Ajay and Prakash is 11 : 10

⇒ Total ratio parts = 11 + 10 = 21 parts

⇒ Value of 21 parts = ₹1218

⇒ Value of 1 part = 1218 / 21 = 58

⇒ Prakash's share (10 parts) = 10 × 58 = ₹580

**∴ The correct answer is ₹580.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

Amount = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ, where P is the principal sum, R is the rate of interest, and n is the time period in years.

Division of Amount in CI

If a total sum is divided into two parts P₁ and P₂ such that their amounts after t₁ and t₂ years respectively at R% CI are equal, then P₁ / P₂ = (1 + R/100)t² − t¹. The person with less time gets a larger share of the principal.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the principal remains constant throughout the period. In Compound Interest, the interest earned in previous periods is added to the principal for the calculation of interest in subsequent periods.
